framework: AWS Inspector v2 + PCI DSS v4.0 Mapping
description: Checklist for auditing AWS Inspector v2 configuration and analyzing detected vulnerabilities, with mappings to relevant PCI DSS controls.

items.title: Inspector v2 NOT enabled in the account
items.description: AWS Inspector v2 is not enabled in the account, leading to a complete lack of automated vulnerability scanning for EC2 instances, ECR container images, and Lambda functions.
items.remediation: Enable AWS Inspector v2 in all relevant regions and ensure it is configured to scan all supported resource types (EC2, ECR, Lambda).

pci_dss.reason: This control requires that security vulnerabilities are identified and managed. Without Inspector v2 enabled, the primary automated tool for identifying infrastructure vulnerabilities is missing.
This control mandates performing internal vulnerability scans. Inspector v2 is a key service for automating these scans within the AWS environment.
The absence of a foundational vulnerability management tool like Inspector v2 significantly weakens the overall risk management program.

items.title: CRITICAL vulnerabilities not remediated
items.description: Critical severity vulnerabilities detected by Inspector v2 remain un-remediated, indicating severe security flaws that could lead to data breaches, unauthorized access, or system compromise.
items.remediation: Prioritize and immediately address all CRITICAL vulnerabilities. This typically involves applying security patches, updating software versions, or implementing compensating controls.

pci_dss.reason: This control requires critical or high-security patches/updates to be installed within one month. Critical vulnerabilities demand even faster remediation to maintain security.
This control mandates that all identified security vulnerabilities and weaknesses are addressed promptly. Unremediated critical findings directly violate this.

items.title: Vulnerabilities in publicly accessible resources
items.description: Vulnerabilities present on resources that are directly accessible from the internet (e.g., EC2 with public IP, internet-facing load balancers) significantly increase the attack surface and risk of exploitation.
items.remediation: Immediately remediate vulnerabilities on publicly accessible resources. If direct patching is not possible, implement temporary compensating controls like WAF rules, restrictive network ACLs, or consider isolating the resource.

pci_dss.reason: This control requires restricting inbound traffic to only what is necessary. Vulnerabilities on publicly accessible resources undermine this by providing an exploitable pathway from untrusted networks.

Public-facing web applications require an automated technical solution (e.g., WAF) to detect and prevent web-based attacks. Vulnerabilities on such resources indicate a heightened need for this protection.

items.title: CVEs with known active exploit (0-day, public PoC)
items.description: Detected vulnerabilities have known and active exploits (e.g., public Proof-of-Concept code or 0-day exploits), indicating an immediate and severe threat of targeted attacks.
items.remediation: Isolate or shut down affected systems if necessary. Apply patches or strong mitigating controls immediately. Monitor for signs of exploitation.

pci_dss.reason: Vulnerabilities with active exploits are by definition critical and must be remediated with the highest urgency, aligning with the requirement for prompt installation of security patches.
This control requires preventing common software attacks. CVEs with known exploits represent immediately exploitable attacks that must be mitigated.

items.title: Vulnerabilities in high-criticality resources (AD, databases, API servers)
items.description: Vulnerabilities found in highly critical resources such as directory services (Active Directory), databases storing sensitive data, or core API servers have a disproportionately high impact on confidentiality, integrity, and availability.
items.remediation: Prioritize remediation for these resources above all others. Implement additional monitoring and access restrictions as temporary measures.

pci_dss.reason: Critical resources often handle sensitive data and require strict adherence to the least privilege principle. Vulnerabilities in these resources compromise the integrity of those access controls.
Hardening standards apply most rigorously to critical systems. Vulnerabilities in these systems indicate a failure in maintaining secure configurations.

items.title: Scanning disabled for EC2 (most used resource)
items.description: Inspector v2 scanning is disabled for EC2 instances, leaving the most common compute resources in AWS unmonitored for software vulnerabilities and configuration exposures.
items.remediation: Enable EC2 scanning for all instances within Inspector v2. Ensure new instances are automatically enrolled for scanning.

pci_dss.reason: Internal vulnerability scanning is a PCI DSS requirement. Disabling scanning for EC2, a core component, creates a critical gap in this requirement.
Prevents the effective identification of security vulnerabilities on EC2 instances.

items.title: Scanning disabled for ECR (private images unaudited)
items.description: Inspector v2 scanning is disabled for ECR repositories, meaning private container images used in critical applications are not being audited for embedded software vulnerabilities.
items.remediation: Enable ECR scanning for all repositories within Inspector v2. Integrate vulnerability scanning into the CI/CD pipeline to prevent vulnerable images from reaching production.

pci_dss.reason: Requires maintaining an inventory of software components and addressing vulnerabilities. Container images are critical software components that must be scanned.
Secure development practices (Requirement 6) extend to ensuring container images are free of known vulnerabilities before deployment.

items.title: HIGH vulnerabilities without remediation plan
items.description: High severity vulnerabilities detected by Inspector v2 lack a defined remediation plan, leading to prolonged exposure to significant risks.
items.remediation: Develop and assign clear remediation plans, including responsible teams and timelines (e.g., within 1 week), for all HIGH severity findings.

pci_dss.reason: All applicable security patches/updates, particularly high-severity ones, must be installed within an appropriate timeframe (e.g., one month). A remediation plan is essential for this.
Requires addressing all identified security vulnerabilities and weaknesses. A lack of a remediation plan indicates a gap in this process.

items.title: Multiple CVEs on same resource (accumulation risk)
items.description: A single resource (e.g., an EC2 instance or container image) presents multiple high-severity CVEs, significantly increasing its overall risk profile due to accumulated vulnerabilities.
items.remediation: Prioritize multi-vulnerability resources for remediation. Consider re-deploying or re-architecting the resource with a hardened base image and up-to-date software.

pci_dss.reason: Risk ranking of vulnerabilities should consider cumulative impact. A resource with multiple CVEs has a higher cumulative impact and should be prioritized for remediation.

items.title: Vulnerabilities in critical service components
items.description: Vulnerabilities exist in components directly supporting critical business services, increasing the likelihood of service disruption or compromise if exploited.
items.remediation: Accelerate remediation efforts for vulnerabilities impacting critical service components. Ensure robust monitoring is in place.

pci_dss.reason: Access to system components is based on need-to-know and least privilege. Vulnerabilities in critical service components undermine the security of these sensitive areas.

items.title: ECR scanning disabled (images not audited)
items.description: Inspector v2 scanning for ECR repositories is disabled, meaning private container images that are critical for applications are not being audited for embedded software vulnerabilities.
items.remediation: Enable ECR scanning for all relevant repositories within Inspector v2. Integrate image scanning into the CI/CD pipeline.

pci_dss.reason: Requires maintaining an inventory of software components and addressing vulnerabilities. Unscanned ECR images create a gap in this process.

items.title: Lambda scanning disabled (code not verified)
items.description: Inspector v2 scanning for Lambda functions is disabled, leaving serverless code unverified for software vulnerabilities and configuration issues.
items.remediation: Enable Lambda scanning for all functions within Inspector v2. Integrate code analysis into the serverless development pipeline.

pci_dss.reason: Bespoke and custom software (which Lambda code often is) must be reviewed for vulnerabilities prior to release. Disabling scanning creates a blind spot.

items.title: Inspector findings uninvestigated for >7 days
items.description: Inspector findings, especially high-severity ones, remain uninvestigated for more than 7 days, indicating a delay in security incident response or vulnerability management processes.
items.remediation: Establish and enforce SLAs for investigating Inspector findings. Integrate Security Hub findings with a ticketing or incident management system for prompt action.

pci_dss.reason: Security events (like high-severity findings) must be investigated immediately. Delayed investigation fails this requirement.
Requires addressing all identified security vulnerabilities and weaknesses in a timely manner.

items.title: Resource with vulnerability unpatched for >30 days
items.description: A resource with a detected vulnerability has not been patched or remediated for over 30 days, increasing the window of exposure and potential for exploitation.
items.remediation: Implement and enforce a patching policy with strict deadlines (e.g., 7-30 days depending on severity). Automate patching where possible.

pci_dss.reason: This control explicitly requires critical or high-security patches/updates to be installed within one month of release. Exceeding 30 days for any vulnerability, especially high-severity, violates this.

items.title: MEDIUM vulnerabilities without remediation timeline
items.description: Medium severity vulnerabilities lack a defined timeline for remediation, potentially leading to an accumulation of technical debt and unaddressed risks over time.
items.remediation: Assign clear remediation timelines for all MEDIUM severity findings (e.g., within 2-4 weeks) and integrate them into project backlogs or maintenance schedules.

pci_dss.reason: All applicable security patches/updates must be installed within an appropriate timeframe. Lack of a timeline hinders this process.

items.title: Scanning enabled but without automated reporting
items.description: Inspector v2 is enabled and performing scans, but its findings are not automatically integrated into reports, dashboards, or external systems, hindering proactive management.
items.remediation: Configure automated reporting mechanisms for Inspector findings, such as sending them to AWS Security Hub, custom dashboards, or exporting them periodically.

pci_dss.reason: Requires monitoring security events and alerting personnel. Automated reporting ensures that findings are visible and actionable.

items.title: Inspector not sending notifications for new findings
items.description: New Inspector findings are not generating active notifications (e.g., via SNS to email/chat), delaying security team awareness and response to emerging vulnerabilities.
items.remediation: Configure Amazon EventBridge rules to trigger SNS notifications for new Inspector findings, especially for CRITICAL and HIGH severities, to alert security personnel.

pci_dss.reason: Alerting for security events is crucial. Lack of notifications directly impacts the ability to respond to new vulnerabilities.

items.title: Resources excluded from scanning without documented justification
items.description: Some resources are explicitly excluded from Inspector v2 scanning without a clear, documented business or technical justification, creating potential blind spots in vulnerability coverage.
items.remediation: Review all excluded resources. Either provide clear, documented justification for their exclusion and any compensating controls, or re-include them in the Inspector v2 scanning scope.

pci_dss.reason: Maintaining an accurate inventory of in-scope system components and understanding why certain components are not monitored is essential for compliance and risk management.

items.title: LOW/INFORMATIONAL vulnerabilities pending
items.description: Low or informational severity vulnerabilities, while not immediately critical, remain unaddressed. These can contribute to technical debt or be part of a larger attack chain.
items.remediation: Address LOW/INFORMATIONAL findings as part of routine maintenance, during resource lifecycle updates, or when patching higher-severity issues on the same resource.

pci_dss.reason: While higher priorities exist, the control implies all applicable security updates should be addressed within an appropriate timeframe, including lower-severity ones.

items.title: Duplicate findings (same vulnerability across multiple resources)
items.description: Multiple instances of the same vulnerability are detected across numerous resources, often indicating a common underlying issue such as an outdated base image, shared library, or system configuration.
items.remediation: Identify the common root cause (e.g., base AMI, Docker image) and implement a centralized fix to efficiently address the vulnerability across all affected resources.

pci_dss.reason: Efficiently identifying and managing security vulnerabilities involves understanding patterns like duplicated findings to address root causes effectively.

items.title: CVEs resolved in newer version but not yet available
items.description: A CVE has a fix available in a newer software version, but that version is not currently compatible or readily deployable in the environment, leading to a temporary inability to fully remediate.
items.remediation: Plan an upgrade path for the affected component, evaluate workarounds, or accept the temporary risk with compensating controls if deemed appropriate after a risk assessment.

pci_dss.reason: Even if a direct patch isn't immediately deployable, the requirement for addressing vulnerabilities means a plan must be in place, or compensating controls justified, for such scenarios.

items.title: Instances with IMDSv1 enabled (SSRF risk -> credential theft)
items.description: EC2 instances that do not require IMDSv2 (HttpTokens != required) are exposed to metadata credential theft in SSRF scenarios.
items.remediation: Enforce IMDSv2 on all EC2 instances by setting HttpTokens=require and review workloads for metadata access compatibility.

pci_dss.reason: Known attack techniques such as SSRF credential theft should be prevented through secure configuration hardening.
Compromised metadata credentials can bypass least-privilege boundaries and expose broader access paths.

items.title: EC2 user-data contains potential secrets or credentials
items.description: User-data scripts include patterns consistent with credentials (keys, tokens, passwords), creating immediate post-compromise exposure.
items.remediation: Remove secrets from user-data, rotate exposed credentials, and move secret retrieval to managed services such as Secrets Manager or Parameter Store.

pci_dss.reason: Sensitive authentication data and credentials must not be exposed in insecure storage locations.
Credential management requires controlled issuance and storage, not plaintext bootstrap scripts.

items.title: Lambda environment variables with sensitive keys
items.description: Lambda environment variables contain keys likely representing secrets, increasing impact of function compromise or log leakage.
items.remediation: Move sensitive values to Secrets Manager/SSM Parameter Store, enable KMS protections, and minimize plaintext secret exposure in runtime configuration.

pci_dss.reason: Sensitive data should be protected and stored using approved secure secret-management mechanisms.
Secure coding and deployment practices must avoid embedding secrets in application configuration.

items.title: Instance profiles with excessive permissions (admin/wildcard)
items.description: EC2 instance profiles include attached policies indicating over-privileged permissions, amplifying impact of workload compromise and lateral movement.
items.remediation: Reduce role permissions to least privilege, remove administrator-equivalent policies from compute roles, and isolate sensitive actions behind scoped roles.

pci_dss.reason: Compute identities must operate with least privilege to limit blast radius upon compromise.
Privileges assigned to system accounts must align with explicit job-function requirements.

items.title: EBS snapshots shared publicly
items.description: EBS snapshots shared with all accounts (public restore permissions) can expose disk contents, credentials, and sensitive data.
items.remediation: Revoke public snapshot sharing, restrict createVolumePermission to specific accounts, and continuously audit snapshot ACLs.

pci_dss.reason: Stored sensitive data must be protected from unauthorized disclosure through backup artifacts.
Snapshot restoration rights must be limited to authorized identities only.

items.title: ECS task definitions with hardcoded secrets in environment variables
items.description: ECS task definitions store sensitive configuration (passwords, tokens, API keys, credentials) as plaintext environment variables in the containerDefinitions.environment block. Any entity with ecs:DescribeTaskDefinition permission can read these values, and they appear in CloudTrail logs and AWS console.
items.remediation: Replace plaintext environment variables with AWS Secrets Manager or SSM Parameter Store references using the containerDefinitions.secrets block. Rotate all exposed credentials immediately.

pci_dss.reason: Sensitive authentication data must not be stored in insecure locations. Plaintext secrets in ECS task definitions are readable by any IAM principal with ecs:DescribeTaskDefinition access.
Secure development and deployment practices must prevent embedding secrets in application configuration artifacts such as container task definitions.
Credential management requires controlled issuance and secure storage, not plaintext values in compute configuration.

notes: Generated based on aws-vuln-skill.md and mapped against PCI DSS v4.0 controls.
